newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish budget sees 1.8 pct 1997 CPI growth - agency.
newsitem.headline: Swedish budget sees 1.8 pct 1997 CPI growth - agency.

text.p: The Swedish government's budget due later on Tuesday will forecast inflation at 1.8 percent in 1997, 1.5 percent in 1998 and 2.0 percent for 1999 and 2000, Swedish national news agency TT reported.
TT said it had obtained an advance copy of the budget, which is often leaked to the press in advance of its publication.
The budget is due to be announced at 1100 GMT.

In the budget, the government expects unemployment to fall to 4.5 percent in 2000 from 7.9 percent in 1997, TT reported. Prime Minister Goran Persson has pledged to halve unemployment to 4.0 percent by 2000 from 1996 levels of around 8.0 percent.
Gross domestic product grew at a modest 1.1 percent in 1996, but would gather speed to expand by 2.3 percent in 1997 and 2.5 percent in 1998, TT quoted the budget document as saying.
Private consumption grew 1.5 percent in 1996 and was forecast to grow 2.0 percent in both 1997 and 1998, TT said.

The budget would also reveal increased spending on old age pensions and employers would be encouraged to employ young unemployed people by being compensated for offering retirement at the age of 63 instead of 64, TT said.
